The federal government's System for Award Management posts a fresh batch of contract opportunities every day, and most of them aren't a fit for any given contractor. Reading through that firehose to find the handful worth pursuing is real business-development time that small teams don't have to spare.

GovChain watches that opportunity feed and scores each incoming notice against a contractor's actual capabilities, attaching a plain-English pursue / monitor / skip call to every score instead of just a keyword match. From there it can auto-draft a starting capability statement, so the write-up isn't beginning from a blank page.

The other half of it: for Made-in-USA and Buy American Act domestic-content claims, GovChain hash-anchors the provenance record to Polygon, so the claim behind a component or product isn't a self-attestation sitting in a PDF somewhere — it's a tamper-evident record anyone can check. It also tracks certification status (ISO 9001, AS9100, CMMC) so a renewal deadline doesn't slip past unnoticed.

If your BD team is still triaging federal opportunity listings by hand, take a look at what automated fit-scoring changes.

reddit.title: Automating federal opportunity triage (SAM listings) with AI fit-scoring — anyone else drowning in irrelevant notices?
reddit.body:
Every notice that lands in the federal System for Award Management gets read by someone on a BD team trying to figure out if it's worth pursuing, and for most small contractors the overwhelming majority aren't a fit. That triage work eats hours that could go into the pursuits that actually matter.

I've been working on GovChain, which scores incoming opportunities against a contractor's stated capabilities and attaches a plain-English pursue / monitor / skip call to each one, rather than just matching keywords in the notice text. It can also auto-draft a starting capability statement once you decide to pursue something.

Separately, for Made-in-USA / Buy American Act domestic-content claims, it hash-anchors the provenance record to Polygon so the claim isn't just sitting in a self-attested PDF — it's something a contracting officer (or anyone else) can independently check. It also tracks certification status (ISO 9001, AS9100, CMMC) so renewals don't sneak up on you.

Curious how others here handle the opportunity firehose today — manual triage, saved searches, something else? Genuinely want to know what's actually working for people.

https://govchain.us/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=govchain-fit-score&utm_content=a

Disclosure: I work on this project.
